title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
wiki_lead:
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is a 2017 action-adventure game developed by Nintendo EPD for the Wii U and Nintendo Switch. Set near the end of the Zelda timeline, it follows Link as he sets out to save Princess Zelda and prevent Calamity Ganon from destroying the world. The player explores the open world of Hyrule, collects items, and completes objectives such as puzzles and side quests. Breath of the Wild's world is unstructured and encourages exploration and experimentation; the story can be completed in a nonlinear fashion.
The five-year development commenced after the release of The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword (2011). Led by the director Hidemaro Fujibayashi and the producer Eiji Aonuma, EPD sought to rethink Zelda's conventions and introduced elements such as detailed chemistry and physics engines. EPD drew inspiration from the original Legend of Zelda (1986), Shadow of the Colossus (2005) and The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011). Monolith Soft, developer of the Xenoblade series, assisted in designing landscapes and topography due to their experience in developing open world games.
Breath of the Wild was released on March 3, 2017, as the final Nintendo-published Wii U game and as a launch title for the Switch. It received acclaim, with praise for its gameplay, open-world design, and attention to detail, though some reviewers criticized its technical performance. Breath of the Wild won numerous year-end accolades, including Game of the Year at the 2017 Game Awards and the 21st Annual D.I.C.E. Awards. It broke sales records for a Nintendo launch game and sold 35.76 million copies by June 2026, making it the bestselling Zelda game and one of the bestselling video games.
Breath of the Wild is considered one of the greatest video games of all time; journalists described it as a landmark in open world design for its emphasis on experimentation, physics-based sandbox, and emergent gameplay. Numerous developers cited Breath of the Wild as inspiration, and it is a popular point of comparison among open-world games. A spinoff, Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity, was released in 2020, and a sequel, The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, was released in 2023. An enhanced version for the Nintendo Switch 2 was released on June 5, 2025.

Gameplay

Breath of the Wild is an open-world action-adventure game. Players are tasked with exploring the kingdom of Hyrule while controlling Link. Breath of the Wild encourages nonlinear gameplay, which is illustrated by the lack of defined entrances or exits to areas, scant instruction given to the player, and encouragement to explore freely. Breath of the Wild introduces a consistent physics engine to the Zelda series, letting players approach problems in different ways rather than trying to find a single solution. grok_lead: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild is an action-adventure video game developed and published by Nintendo Entertainment Planning & Development (EPD) for the Wii U and Nintendo Switch consoles. Released worldwide on March 3, 2017, it marks a pivotal entry in the long-running The Legend of Zelda series, introducing an expansive open-world design that emphasizes player freedom, exploration, and survival mechanics in the vast kingdom of Hyrule. Players control the protagonist Link, who awakens from a century-long slumber in the Shrine of Resurrection, amnesiac and tasked with regaining his strength to confront the malevolent Calamity Ganon that has devastated the land. The game's gameplay revolves around nonlinear exploration, where Link can climb nearly any surface, glide with a paraglider, cook meals from foraged ingredients, and wield improvised weapons in dynamic combat encounters. Environmental interactions play a central role, allowing players to solve puzzles using physics-based mechanics, such as manipulating fire, electricity, or wind to navigate shrinesâover 100 ancient trials scattered across Hyrule that reward abilities and equipment. Survival elements require managing stamina, health, and inventory while adapting to diverse biomes, from arid deserts to snowy mountains, often without traditional hand-holding tutorials or linear progression. An Expansion Pass adds new challenges, including a DLC storyline titled The Champions' Ballad, which expands on the base game's lore and mechanics. Set in a post-apocalyptic version of Hyrule, the narrative unfolds through fragmented memories and interactions with remnants of the kingdom's fallen champions, blending high fantasy with themes of loss and resilience. Link's journey involves allying with four divine beasts, ancient machines that once defended Hyrule, and assembling tools like the Sheikah Slate for traversal and combat. The story draws from the series' mythology but prioritizes emergent player-driven narratives over scripted events, allowing multiple paths to the final confrontation with Ganon at Hyrule Castle. Development began in 2013 under director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, evolving from an initial Wii U project influenced by The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword but pivoting toward open-world innovation inspired by real-world travel and non-linear design philosophies. Monolith Soft provided support for the game's expansive world-building, resulting in over 100 square kilometers of explorable terrain generated with procedural elements for variety. Delayed from 2015 to refine its ambitious scope, the title launched alongside the Nintendo Switch, with an enhanced port for the Nintendo Switch 2 released on June 5, 2025, featuring performance upgrades. Upon release, Breath of the Wild received universal acclaim, earning a 97/100 Metacritic score for the Switch version based on 117 critic reviews praising its revolutionary open-world freedom and immersive design. It won multiple Game of the Year awards, including at The Game Awards 2017 and from outlets like IGN, and has sold 33.34 million copies worldwide as of September 2025, making it one of Nintendo's best-selling titles. The game's influence extends to the broader industry, redefining open-world conventions by prioritizing curiosity-driven discovery over quest markers, impacting subsequent titles in exploration-focused gameplay.
